# SasaVenos Recommends No More Than 30 To 40 Seconds Of Banded Skill Volume Per Session After His Own Maltese Trial

After his own five-week maltese trial on rings, SasaVenos recommends a band that keeps the skill at 80 to 90 percent of the one rep max, and no more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Details

- In his trial he trained only holds in his 80 to 90 percent rep max, which he puts at 8 to 16 seconds and 4 to 8 reps. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He did maltese with the light band and trained rings twice per week. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He did around 10 sets of holds per week. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- His result: from 8.5 seconds with band to 11 seconds "of body [bodyweight]" maltese hold in five weeks. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- The hard part was not doing any heavier loads until a predetermined day, only with the band, even though he could do it with his body weight. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- His conclusion: use only the rubber band that takes away five to nine kilograms, and do not do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- If the volume sounds like too little, he says to decrease the rest between sets until you are doing it super efficiently and quickly. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He says to apply progressive overload to your sets and try to work a little bit harder every week, but do not increase the volume. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He says that this is his opinion and that the viewer is "allowed to disagree". [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Evidence

- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "perform movements and isometrics that are in my 80 to 90 percent rep max that is 8 to 16 seconds and 4 to 8 reps and that means that i need to only do maltese with the light band and so i train rings twice per week only around 10 sets of holds per week"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "i got from 8.5 seconds with band to 11 seconds of body [bodyweight] with maltese hold in just five weeks"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "the hard part was not doing any heavier loads until a predetermined day only with the band even though i could do it with my body weight and record cool clips and be cool but i really wanted to try this out and it worked amazingly"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "but this is my conclusion change progressions of a skill that's in 80 to 90 percent of your one rep max use only the rubber band that takes away five to nine kilograms don't do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "if it sounds like too little then decrease the rest between sets until you're doing it super efficiently and quickly apply progressive overload to your sets try to work a little bit harder every week but do not increase the volume"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "of course this is my opinion and you're allowed to disagree with me"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "maxing out my three seconds of maltese and five seconds of cross every single session wondering why i can't make any progress ... so the whole time i'm training in the 95 to 100 of my rep max wondering what's wrong"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "i got from it was a ton of frustration and bicep tendon irritation"

## Example From The Source

His own maltese hold went from 8.5 seconds with the band to 11 seconds "of body [bodyweight]" in five weeks of this plan. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Why This Matters

He says that before this plan he maxed out his maltese and cross holds every single session, trained "in the 95 to 100 of my rep max", made no progress, and got bicep tendon irritation. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
